title: Maximum Area Rectangle With Point Constraints II
summary: Given n points on an infinite plane with coordinates in xCoord and yCoord, find the largest rectangle with sides parallel to the axes that includes exactly four points as vertices and no other points inside or on its border.
statement: Given n points on an infinite plane with coordinates in xCoord and yCoord, find the largest rectangle with sides parallel to the axes that includes exactly four points as vertices and no other points inside or on its border. Return the area of this rectangle or -1 if no such rectangle exists.
constraints: x_coord and y_coord describe up to 200,000 unique points with coordinates in 0..80,000,000.
A valid positive-area axis-aligned rectangle uses four points as corners and has no other point inside or on its border.
hints: A valid rectangle uses adjacent y-pairs in both boundary columns.
Sweep columns while a range-maximum tree records the latest x seen at every y.
For each adjacent pair, require the same prior adjacent pair and no later x anywhere across its closed y-range.
These checks exclude all four borders and the interior; every empty rectangle is discovered at its right boundary.
editorial: These checks exclude all four borders and the interior; every empty rectangle is discovered at its right boundary.

tests.explanation: The four points form an empty two-by-two rectangle with area four.
The center point invalidates the only rectangle, so return -1.
